title: Rabbah bar Chiyya Ketosfa’ah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav’s student, citing [Bava Batra 93b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.93b.15): “Rava bar Chiyya Ketosfa’ah in Rav’s name: One who picks pebbles from his fellow’s threshing floor,” etc.

So it is in [Yerushalmi Kilayim, beginning of chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.2.1.3-4): “Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, Abba son of Rabbi Chiyya in the name of Rav: One who picks pebbles,” etc. The statement is cited in [Beitzah 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.38b.3), and there the words “Rabbah bar” are missing.

In [Yevamot 104a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.104a.7), Rabbah bar Chiyya Ketosfa’ah performed chalitzah before Shmuel, and Shmuel said of him: “How great is this man’s strength, that he follows an individual opinion” (see [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yevamot.104a.7.2)).

[Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3161&lang=en) cites that Rav Sherira Gaon wrote: “In those years when Rabbah bar Nachmani was in Pumbedita, Rabbah bar Chiyya was spreading Torah in Sura.” Hyman objects, with respect, that he overlooked an error in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, and Hyman proposes reading there Rabbah bar Rav Huna, as in the B.G. and London versions, as explained in his entry and in the entry Rabbah.[^3]

notes.text: כיחידאי means following an individual opinion rather than the majority. Hyman’s proposed Rabbah bar Rav Huna correction of the Epistle and the competing Rava/Rabbah forms retain their attribution.

Yevamot 104a directly explains following an individual opinion. The proposed Epistle correction and competing Seder Ha Dorot/B.G./London readings remain Hyman-attributed; those exact editions were not independently inspected.

The consulted Bava Batra reads Rabbah as the authority, with the compensation ruling finishing at [Bava Batra 94a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.94a.1). Kilayim and Beitzah give Rav. Heilprin reports Rav in the Rif and Rosh. Rashi takes Shmuel’s remark in Yevamot as criticism. Both Heilprin and [the consulted Epistle](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.100) have Rabbah bar Chiyya teaching in Sura. Hyman prefers Rabbah bar Rav Huna, citing distinct editions.
